messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] compile PDF from an Rnw file
parts:
This is not valid:

d4[d4$X1>=8,] [,-c("X3", "X4", "X5")]

You can only use `-` before numeric indices; R does not know what
negative character strings mean.

Regards,
Yihui

On Sun, Dec 2, 2012 at 9:52 PM, Pradip <pradip....@gmail.com> wrote:
> keep_var <- c("X1", "X2")
> drop_var <- c("X3", "X4", "X5")
>
> N <- 100
> set.seed(13)
> df<-data.frame(matrix(sample(c(1:10,NA),N, replace=TRUE),ncol=5))
>
> d4[d4$X1>=8,] [,1:2]
> d4[d4$X1>=8,] [,-c(3,4,5)]
> d4[d4$X1>=8,] [,c(-3,-4,-5)]
> d4[d4$X1>=8,] [,c("X1", "X2")]
> d4[d4$X1>=8,] [,-c("X3", "X4", "X5")] # does not work, see the
> alternative below
> d4[d4$X1>=8,][-which(names(df)%in% c("X3","X4","X5"))]
> d4[d4$X1>=8,] [,keep_var]
> d4[d4$X1>=8,] [, !drop_var] # does not work, see the
> alternative below
> d4[d4$X1>=8,][,!names(df)%in%drop_var]

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] compile PDF from an Rnw file
parts:
1. If an error happens, the results up to that point will be written
out; please check the *.tex file;

2. If I'm to guess what happened from the error message, it is
probably a file not found; remember the base directory of your code
chunk is the same directory as your Rnw file; since there is no
reproducible example, nothing else can be said;

3. At the moment I do not have such plans, but I'm open to such
opportunities (i.e. I may accept invitations).

Regards,
Yihui
